newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bill price rise to slow down on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bill price rise to slow down on Monday.

text.p: The price rise of Russian GKO discount Treasury bills, spurred in the morning by Central Bank refinancing rate cuts, will cool down on Monday as banks need a lot of funds for next week's auctions, dealers said on Friday.
The Finance Ministry will offer a record 20 trillion roubles of T-bills and OFZ interest-bearing bonds at auction on June 18.
The Central Bank said on Friday it would cut its refinancing rate to 24 percent from 36 percent from June 16, sending yields on long-term T-bills to record lows of below 20 percent.
Dealers said the rise will be capped as foreign investors would not accept yields of less than 20 percent.
*Average yield fell to 18.97 from 19.90 percent on Tuesday
*Turnover fell to 5.02 trillion roubles from 5.33 trillion roubles
*Central Bank placed three OFZ bonds worth 207.05 billion roubles

"Next week banks will be getting ready for auctions with a huge issue volume for which each primary dealer will have to transfer about 200 billion roubles," Natsionaly Rezervny Bank dealer Stanislav Litvinov. "If the Central Bank does not cut the requirement, banks will either have to borrow in the interbank market, or sell paper."
He said banks would first of all sell short paper as prices were rising.

"There is no point in selling long-term paper before the auction as there is a real chance not to buy anything at all, or to buy at an average price at a lower yield, judging by the latest auctions," he said.
At the last auction on Wednesday non-residents, or the state bank Sberbank bought most of the issues at non-competitive bids, leaving most Russian banks out of the deal.

Dealers said foreign interest in the government paper was weakening. Russian companies, anxious to invest roubles they receive as the economy is dedollarising, are behind the new cash inflow, they said.
